findings.summary: _REBUILT_BRIEF_NAMES re-declares the set of brief names a launch re-composes that recovery_review_subject.materialize_run_review_brief already owns at recovery_review_subject.py:634; a third rebuilt-brief name added to the owner would be missed by is_rebuilt_brief, and the queue would freeze it as a steering copy again, which is the defect this delta fixes.
the skip-removal control's row closes with a stray after its , so the delivered evidence table carries malformed markup and a parser sees a cell outside any row.

the skip-removal control is reported as measured (3 failed, 6 passed) but no log for it exists under the run directory — only negative-control.log, which records the launch-rebind mutation — so a later reader cannot verify the second control's numbers.

the after_suite command is truncated at the nonexistent tests/test_a_jev_hold_queues_placeholder.py and embeds a literal (serial) token, so it is not the command that ran; the gate log's own header carries the full list, but the machine-read block and the receipt differ.

raw_text: VERDICT goal: the source goal is that a queued request's brief binds at launch from steering.md in its own run directory; the delta keeps reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:_launch_queued rebinding node.brief/brief_path to the steering file and adds reckon/crew/runs.py:596 is_rebuilt_brief so a brief the launch re-composes is never frozen by the launch path. VERDICT done_when: the done_when names a new tests/test_queue_steering_binding.py plus zero added failures against the base revision; the delta adds three arms to that module, and I re-ran it at a054a27a in a git-archive scratch tree (review-gate.log: 9 passed, EXIT=0), while the recorded serial head and base arms (gate-head-serial.log 373 passed/4 failed, gate-base-serial.log 364 passed/4 failed) carry the same four failure ids, so the added count is zero. VERDICT write_paths: the source node's seven declared paths include reckon/crew/runs.py, reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py, tests/test_queue_steering_binding.py and the evidence fragment, and every path in git diff --stat 13cc1960a..a054a27a (four files) is one of them. VERDICT manifest: read; it records commits ac35abf17 and a054a27a8 plus the earlier three, both suite blocks, the negative control and its three red arms, and a checkpoint recorded at 09:07 before the closing evidence commit, but its after_suite command line is truncated to a placeholder filename (manifest.md:19). VERDICT diff: read commit by commit against 13cc1960a; ac35abf17 moves the brief byte-copy into runs.store_brief, has dispatch_admission._store_brief delegate to it, adds is_rebuilt_brief and its skip in runs._write_steering, and adds three test arms; a054a27a8 changes the evidence fragment only, so the code at the reviewed head is ac35abf17's. SCORE durability: 18 JUSTIFICATION durability: tests/test_queue_steering_binding.py:309 would redden if runs._write_steering took a steering copy of a composed review brief (its no-steering assertion and its stale-digest inequality), :375 would redden if the inside-run-directory skip were removed, and :402 would error if the OSError guard at runs.py:642 were removed; negative-control.log shows the launch-rebind mutation reddening three arms. SCORE fit: 18 JUSTIFICATION fit: store_brief, is_rebuilt_brief and _REBUILT_BRIEF_NAMES at reckon/crew/runs.py:555 name the mechanism with no plan, stage or ticket reference, and the delegate in reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:2244 follows the surrounding lazy-import idiom. SCORE reuse: 15 JUSTIFICATION reuse: reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:2244 now delegates to reckon/crew/runs.py:559 store_brief, resolving the prior duplication of the byte-copy, but reckon/crew/runs.py:555 re-declares the composed-brief name set recovery_review_subject.py:634 already owns.
